lua/bot-heuristics.candidate: Header order is parsed from the raw request block, lowercased, rather than from the header map
Order penalty counts inversions instead of a longest increasing subsequence
Fewer than three known headers are not judged for order
The total score is capped at 1
Score and reasons stored on the request context for access logging
Would-reject recorded per module in a shared context map so several log-only modules all show up
Operator options merge over the defaults
TLS family taken from operator option or X-JA3-Family header

lua/geo-asn.candidate: ipv4_to_int rejects octets above 255 and malformed addresses
/0 range matches every IPv4 address; invalid prefix lengths never match
List entries compared as strings so numeric and string ASNs both match
Decision reason stored in ngx.ctx.geo_reason and waf_rejected / waf_would_reject flags
Allowed client in an allowed country passes even if country listed on denylist too (allowlist wins)
A client inside an allowed address range is always admitted
A client inside a denied address range is refused even from an allowed country or network
IPv6 clients are not matched by address ranges and fall through to country and network rules
Country and network allow and deny lists decide whether a client is admitted
Traffic no rule matches is admitted or refused according to the default posture
An enforced refusal returns the configured status and logs it as rejected
In log-only mode a client the policy would refuse is admitted and logged as would-reject

lua/jwt.candidate: base64url decoding and padding rules
HMAC-SHA256 built from resty.sha256 per RFC 2104
Constant-time signature comparison
Key set cached in a shared dict for jwks_ttl so one fetch serves all workers
Key set fetch uses a 2-second timeout and an overridable fetch function
Verified claims published to later phases via ngx.ctx.jwt; ngx.ctx.waf_rejected / waf_would_reject markers
"Bearer " prefix is optional and case-insensitive on the first letter
Token header name and rejection status are configurable
Each log-only module that would reject is recorded alongside others
A correctly signed, current token reaches the upstream
A request without a verifiable token is refused with 401
A token naming an algorithm the deployment does not accept is refused
A token outside its validity window, beyond the tolerated skew, is refused
A token from another issuer or for another audience is refused
A token with no expiry is accepted indefinitely
A token is checked only against the published key it names
When the published key set cannot be obtained, public-key tokens are refused
The upstream receives the subject of a verified token
A subject header sent by the client reaches the upstream unchanged when the edge forwards none
In log-only mode, a request without a valid token is let through and recorded as a would-reject
When enforcing, a refused request is logged as rejected, never as log-only

lua/mirror.candidate: Kill switch result is cached per worker and can be reset by a reload hook (reset_kill_cache)
Request body is read when a request is mirrored and max_body > 0
Decision and reason stored in the request context (dc_mirror, dc_reason)
Gate variable name dc_mirror and the 204 short-circuit in the shadow location
Random fallback correlation id when nginx has no request_id
Capture fields path, method, status, latency_ms and at
Empty or nil URI and body pass through scrubbing unchanged
Collector request format (Host, Content-Type, Connection: close, default timeout 1000 ms)
A capture that fails JSON encoding is silently dropped
Requests that could write are never mirrored by default
Only the configured share of eligible requests is mirrored
Credential headers are redacted in captured requests and responses
Secret query parameters are redacted in captured URLs
Chosen JSON body fields are redacted in captured response bodies
A captured response body over the size cap is truncated and marked as truncated

lua/ratelimit.candidate: State serialised into the shared dict as pipe/comma strings and decoded back
Idle limit state expires after a TTL of twice its longest relevant period
Cross-worker over-admit of about (workers - 1) requests under a concurrent burst
Sliding log keeps at most capacity timestamps
Token bucket refills at rate and never past capacity after idle; leaky bucket drains at rate
Defaults: token-bucket, capacity 20, rate 10, window 1, dict waf_ratelimit
Long and short spellings of an algorithm count in separate quotas

lua/ratelimit.rule: A rate limit is one quota per client across all nginx workers, not one per worker
